answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake before it may place jobs or earn reputation. A challenge period lets peers flag duplicate-controlled accounts; proven Sybils lose their stake, while honest newcomers recover it after behaving normally. This does not prove one human per agent, but makes mass identity creation costly: an attacker must lock capital in every account and risks losing it. A sonnet from a hollow profile, signed with a quill, earns no exemption.
